lessons.title: From a table to a straight-line graph
lessons.summary: Substitute signed inputs, plot their ordered pairs to scale and read coordinates back from a line.
lessons.objective: Substitute signed inputs, plot their ordered pairs to scale and read coordinates back from a line.
lessons.before: Read an ordered pair as horizontal coordinate first and vertical coordinate second.
lessons.ideas:
For a rule of the form \(y=ax+b\), first multiply by \(a\) and then add \(b\). A negative input belongs inside brackets when you substitute.

Start at the x-coordinate, then move to the y-height. Use crosses for the table points. When the rule is linear, join the points with one straight line.

Follow a grid line to reach the graph, then read the missing coordinate on the other axis. A line intersection is the ordered pair shared by both lines.
lessons.method:
How do I make a table of values?

Each column pairs one x-value with its output. Substitute that number into the rule everywhere x occurs.

How do I place each point on the grid?

Find the distance between two numbered grid lines. Count the smaller divisions on each axis separately.

How do I read an input, output or intersection?

When x is given, start on the horizontal axis. When y is given, start on the vertical axis.
mistakes: The first value in the pair is x even when it is negative. Do not reorder the pair to put the positive number first.
An equal distance on the paper need not represent an equal number of x-units and y-units.
A horizontal line holds y constant. Its different points still have different x-values.

examples.title: Complete a table for an increasing straight line
examples.question:
Complete the missing entries in the table for \(y=2x+1\).

\(x\)\(-2\)\(-1\)\(0\)\(1\)\(2\)
\(y\)\(-3\)?\(1\)?\(5\)
examples.solution:
Multiply the x-value by the coefficient of x, then add the constant.

For \(x=-1\), substitute that input into the rule. It gives \(y=-1\).

For \(x=1\), substitute that input into the rule. It gives \(y=3\).

\(x\)\(-2\)\(-1\)\(0\)\(1\)\(2\)
\(y\)\(-3\)\(-1\)\(1\)\(3\)\(5\)

examples.title: Read the vertical value on a straight line
examples.question: The graph shows \(y=x-2\). Read the value of \(y\) at \(x=1\).
examples.solution:
Find \(x=1\) on the horizontal scale.

Move vertically to the graph and then horizontally to the vertical scale. The point is \(\left(1,-1\right)\).

examples.title: Read both coordinates at a line intersection
examples.question: Read the coordinates where the graphs of \(y=x+1\) and \(y=-2x+4\) meet.
examples.solution:
Find the point common to both lines. It has the same x- and y-coordinates on both graphs.

Read the horizontal value first and the vertical value second. The point is \(\left(1,2\right)\).

lessons.title: Plot and read quadratic graphs
lessons.summary: Make tables for positive and negative quadratic rules, plot a smooth curve and read heights or intercepts.
lessons.objective: Make tables for positive and negative quadratic rules, plot a smooth curve and read heights or intercepts.
lessons.before: Square a negative input inside brackets. Keep a minus sign in front of a squared term outside the square.
lessons.ideas:
At \(x=-2\), the term \(-x^2\) is \(-(-2)^2=-4\). The term \(3x\) is \(3(-2)=-6\). Add the terms only after giving each its sign.

Join the plotted crosses with a single smooth curve. If values at opposite distances from the middle line are equal, use that as a check on the table and the drawing.

Read the x-coordinate of each crossing. For roots, the height is zero. An intercept is the coordinate pair on the axis, while the root itself is its x-value.
lessons.method:
How do I handle a negative value in a squared term?

A negative input gives a positive square. A separate minus sign in front of that square still makes its term negative.

How do I join the plotted points?

Each pair in a quadratic table locates a cross. A smooth quadratic may curve between the printed x-values.

What do I report when one height meets the curve twice?

For a stated height, scan the whole plotted curve on a horizontal line at that height. A single height can give two inputs.
mistakes: For a rule such as \(y=3-x^2\), a negative input does not make the squared term positive after the outer subtraction.
A row of short straight segments can cut through the true curve and change where it meets an axis or another line.
Reading only the first crossing can omit a second valid solution on the other side.

examples.title: Substitute negative inputs in an upward quadratic
examples.question:
Complete the missing entries in the table for \(y=x^{2}+2x-2\).

\(x\)\(-3\)\(-2\)\(-1\)\(0\)\(1\)
\(y\)?\(-2\)\(-3\)?\(1\)
examples.solution:
Put each negative input in brackets before squaring. Evaluate the squared and linear terms separately.

For \(x=-3\), substitute that input into the rule. It gives \(y=1\).

For \(x=0\), substitute that input into the rule. It gives \(y=-2\).

\(x\)\(-3\)\(-2\)\(-1\)\(0\)\(1\)
\(y\)\(1\)\(-2\)\(-3\)\(-2\)\(1\)

examples.title: Read a quadratic height from the two scales
examples.question: The graph shows \(y=x^{2}-2x+3\). Read the value of \(y\) at \(x=2\).
examples.solution:
Find \(x=2\) on the horizontal scale.

Move vertically to the graph and then horizontally to the vertical scale. The point is \(\left(2,3\right)\).

examples.title: Read the two x-intercepts of a quadratic
examples.question: Use the graph of \(y=x^{2}+4x+3\) to estimate the x-values when \(y=0\). Give your answers to one decimal place.
examples.solution:
Use the horizontal axis, where \(y=0\).

Project each intersection onto the x-axis. The readings in order are approximately \(-3.0,\quad -1.0\).

lessons.title: Plot and read reciprocal graphs
lessons.summary: Evaluate a reciprocal table for nonzero inputs, draw its two branches and read coordinate pairs.
lessons.objective: Evaluate a reciprocal table for nonzero inputs, draw its two branches and read coordinate pairs.
lessons.before: Know that a nonzero number divided by a negative number has the opposite sign.
lessons.ideas:
Leave the entry at \(x=0\) undefined. Compute the values for negative and positive inputs separately before plotting.

Leave a gap between the branches at the vertical axis. With a negative numerator, positive and negative inputs still give opposite signs, but the two branches switch their vertical positions.

Read the other coordinate using its own scale. Outputs close to zero may need inputs of larger magnitude or a finer vertical scale.
lessons.method:
Why does zero have no table value?

In \(y=\frac{a}{x}\), the input is the number underneath the fraction bar. The rule works for every nonzero input.

How do I draw both sides of the graph?

Draw the negative-input branch using its table values, then draw the positive-input branch. Each branch is continuous over its own set of inputs.

How do I read the correct branch at a given height?

For a given x-value, read only the branch on that side of the vertical axis. For a given y-value, consider which side of the horizontal axis contains the desired height.
mistakes: Writing zero as the output at this missing input would put a false point on the graph.
A line through the origin would add a value where the reciprocal is undefined.
A reciprocal output may be a fraction. Check the divisions before reading its sign or approximate size.

examples.title: Complete a positive reciprocal table on both sides
examples.question:
Complete the missing entries in the table for \(y=\frac{4}{x}\) for \(x\ne0\).

\(x\)\(-4\)\(-2\)\(-1\)\(1\)\(2\)\(4\)
\(y\)\(-1\)?\(-4\)?\(2\)\(1\)
examples.solution:
Divide the numerator by the signed input. Values at opposite nonzero inputs have opposite signs.

For \(x=-2\), substitute that input into the rule. It gives \(y=-2\).

For \(x=1\), substitute that input into the rule. It gives \(y=4\).

\(x\)\(-4\)\(-2\)\(-1\)\(1\)\(2\)\(4\)
\(y\)\(-1\)\(-2\)\(-4\)\(4\)\(2\)\(1\)

examples.title: Handle the excluded input in a reciprocal table
examples.question:
The rule is \(y=\frac{3}{x}\) for \(x\ne0\). What belongs in the table at \(x=0\)?

  1. No value
  2. \(0\)
  3. \(3\)
examples.solution:
Substituting zero gives a denominator of \(0\).

Division by zero is undefined. Leave that cell unavailable and the two branches separate.

examples.title: Read an input at a reciprocal height
examples.question: The graph shows \(y=\frac{-4}{x}\) for \(x\ne0\). Use the graph to find \(x\) when \(y=2\).
examples.solution:
Read the vertical axis at \(y=2\).

Move horizontally to the graph, then down or up to the x-axis. The reading is \(x=-2\).

lessons.title: Use graphs to solve equations
lessons.summary: Estimate all roots and intersections, and choose a comparison line for a related equation.
lessons.objective: Estimate all roots and intersections, and choose a comparison line for a related equation.
lessons.before: Be able to read both axes and trace a plotted curve between table values.
lessons.ideas:
Mark the positions where the curve meets the x-axis. Project these points onto its numbered scale. Give the x-values, keeping every solution in the stated interval.

Read each intersection with the curve. For example, to use \(y=x^2-x+1\) to solve \(x^2-x-2=0\), add 3 to make the comparison \(y=3\).

Plot the expression on the other side as a second line. For solutions in x, read the x-values of the intersections. When asked for intersection points, give their full ordered pairs.
lessons.method:
Where do I look for roots on a graph?

An equation of the form \(f(x)=0\) asks when the graph of the rule is on the horizontal axis. It can cross or touch that axis.

Which line gives a specified output?

An equation of the form \(f(x)=k\) asks when the curve has height \(k\). Draw the horizontal line at that height.

When do I need a sloping comparison line?

If a related equation contains x-terms outside the supplied function, rearrange so one side is exactly the plotted expression.
mistakes: The curve meeting the vertical axis tells you its output at zero. That is only a root if the output there is also zero.
A pencilled guide from an intersection goes vertically to the x-axis. A horizontal guide goes to the y-axis and gives the output.
A line with the correct intercept but wrong slope can look close and give different roots. Use two points to draw it accurately.

examples.title: Estimate two roots from the x-axis
examples.question: Use the graph of \(y=x^{2}+4x+1\) to estimate the x-values when \(y=0\). Give your answers to one decimal place.
examples.solution:
Use the horizontal axis, where \(y=0\).

Project each intersection onto the x-axis. The readings in order are approximately \(-3.7,\quad -0.3\).

examples.title: Match a changed equation to the right horizontal line
examples.question: The graph shows \(y=x^{2}+2x+2\) and a horizontal comparison line. Use them to solve \(x^{2}+2x-2=0\) to one decimal place.
examples.solution:
The requested equation is equivalent to \(x^{2}+2x+2=4\). Read where the curve meets \(y=4\).

Project each intersection onto the x-axis. The readings in order are approximately \(-2.7,\quad 0.7\).

examples.title: Read the root in the plotted interval
examples.question: Only the part of \(y=x^{2}-2\) with \(0\leq x\leq 4\) is shown. Estimate the solution of \(x^{2}-2=0\) on that interval to one decimal place.
examples.solution:
Use the horizontal axis, where \(y=0\).

Project the intersection onto the x-axis. The reading is approximately \(1.4\).

lessons.title: Cubic graphs and sums of powers (Extended)
lessons.summary: Build tables for cubic rules and combinations of powers, plot them smoothly and find their numerical solutions.
lessons.objective: Build tables for cubic rules and combinations of powers, plot them smoothly and find their numerical solutions.
lessons.before: Evaluate a square and a cube at the same negative input, and note their different signs.
lessons.ideas:
At \(x=-2\), \(x^3=-8\) and \(x^2=4\). An outside negative coefficient changes the sign after evaluating the power.

A smooth curve should pass through the calculated points on the stated interval. The rest of the curve can lie outside the printed window.

Plot the line to scale. Read the x-value of each intersection. A cubic can give several distinct readings on the same horizontal level or sloping line.
lessons.method:
How do the terms contribute to a cubic table?

A cubic table can include a cube, a squared or linear term, and a constant. Work through all the terms at the same input before moving to the next column.

Where can I add useful table points?

Plot a point for each column. Check whether the curve changes direction between adjacent positions and calculate more values near a bend if needed.

How do I find every intersection with a line?

Use the steps from graphical equations. Rewrite the requested equation as the given rule equal to a line.
mistakes: A positive number from the square does not make the whole output positive. Combine the signed contributions.
Several points may have the same y-value. They belong at different x-positions.
Stopping after the first crossing loses other solutions. A root at zero should be included when it satisfies the equation.

examples.title: Complete a table for a cubic and a constant
examples.question:
Complete the missing entries in the table for \(y=-\frac{1}{2}x^{3}-1\).

\(x\)\(-2\)\(-1\)\(0\)\(1\)\(2\)
\(y\)\(3\)?\(-1\)\(-\frac{3}{2}\)?
examples.solution:
Cubing a negative input gives a negative result. Apply the outside coefficient after cubing.

For \(x=-1\), substitute that input into the rule. It gives \(y=-\frac{1}{2}\).

For \(x=2\), substitute that input into the rule. It gives \(y=-5\).

\(x\)\(-2\)\(-1\)\(0\)\(1\)\(2\)
\(y\)\(3\)\(-\frac{1}{2}\)\(-1\)\(-\frac{3}{2}\)\(-5\)

examples.title: Read cubic mixtures with a squared term
examples.question:
Complete the missing entries in the table for \(y=-x^{3}+x^{2}-2\).

\(x\)\(-2\)\(-1\)\(0\)\(1\)\(2\)
\(y\)?\(0\)\(-2\)\(-2\)?
examples.solution:
At a negative input, the square is positive but the cube is negative before its outside sign.

For \(x=-2\), substitute that input into the rule. It gives \(y=10\).

For \(x=2\), substitute that input into the rule. It gives \(y=-6\).

\(x\)\(-2\)\(-1\)\(0\)\(1\)\(2\)
\(y\)\(10\)\(0\)\(-2\)\(-2\)\(-6\)

examples.title: Find all displayed roots of a cubic
examples.question: Use the graph of \(y=x^{3}-2x\) to estimate the x-values when \(y=0\). Give your answers to one decimal place.
examples.solution:
Use the horizontal axis, where \(y=0\).

Project each intersection onto the x-axis. The readings in order are approximately \(-1.4,\quad 0.0,\quad 1.4\).

lessons.title: Root and negative-power graphs (Extended)
lessons.summary: Plot square-root, reciprocal-square-root and inverse-square rules, including sums of powers with gaps.
lessons.objective: Plot square-root, reciprocal-square-root and inverse-square rules, including sums of powers with gaps.
lessons.before: A square root is the nonnegative value whose square is the input. A denominator cannot be zero.
lessons.ideas:
Write \(x^{\frac12}=\sqrt{x}\quad\text{and}\quad x^{-\frac12}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}\). The reciprocal needs strictly positive inputs because its denominator cannot be zero.

For \(y=ax^{-2}=\frac{a}{x^2}\), both signs of a nonzero input are allowed and have the same square. The two branches do not join at zero.

In \(y=\frac2x+\frac4{x^2}\), use nonzero inputs, including both signs. The two terms can have different signs for a negative input.
lessons.method:
Which inputs do the two root rules allow?

A positive half power means the real nonnegative square root. Its input must be at least zero.

How do I plot an inverse square?

A power of minus two gives the reciprocal of the square. Compute the squared input before division.

What if two different powers appear together?

Read each term to see which inputs are allowed. Use only inputs that make all terms defined, then calculate the terms independently.
mistakes: A missing negative-input branch for a square-root rule is not a drawing omission. The real rule cannot give those outputs.
A reciprocal square is distinct from the ordinary reciprocal. Opposite inputs have equal outputs, not opposite outputs, in this rule.
Do not combine the two denominators mentally before checking whether the original rule allows the input.

examples.title: Plot a positive square-root rule
examples.question:
Complete the missing entries in the table for \(y=x^{\frac{1}{2}}\) for \(x\geq0\).

\(x\)\(0\)\(1\)\(4\)\(9\)\(16\)
\(y\)\(0\)?\(2\)?\(4\)
examples.solution:
The half power is the nonnegative square root. This rule includes x equal to zero.

For \(x=1\), substitute that input into the rule. It gives \(y=1\).

For \(x=9\), substitute that input into the rule. It gives \(y=3\).

\(x\)\(0\)\(1\)\(4\)\(9\)\(16\)
\(y\)\(0\)\(1\)\(2\)\(3\)\(4\)

examples.title: Read both sides of a reciprocal-square function
examples.question:
Complete the missing entries in the table for \(y=\frac{4}{x^{2}}\) for \(x\ne0\).

\(x\)\(-4\)\(-2\)\(-1\)\(1\)\(2\)\(4\)
\(y\)\(\frac{1}{4}\)?\(4\)?\(1\)\(\frac{1}{4}\)
examples.solution:
The denominator is the square of x, so opposite inputs have the same denominator and output.

For \(x=-2\), substitute that input into the rule. It gives \(y=1\).

For \(x=1\), substitute that input into the rule. It gives \(y=4\).

\(x\)\(-4\)\(-2\)\(-1\)\(1\)\(2\)\(4\)
\(y\)\(\frac{1}{4}\)\(1\)\(4\)\(4\)\(1\)\(\frac{1}{4}\)

examples.title: Identify inputs that a root-based graph allows
examples.question:
Which stated set of inputs gives real outputs for \(y=\frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}\)?

  1. \(x\gt0\)
  2. \(x\geq0\)
  3. \(x\lt0\)
  4. All real inputs
examples.solution:
A real square root requires \(x\geq0\).

The reciprocal also excludes zero because it would make the denominator zero.

The allowed inputs are \(x\gt0\).

lessons.title: Exponential graphs, growth and decay (Extended)
lessons.summary: Build exponential tables and use a scaled graph to read initial values and growth or decay thresholds.
lessons.objective: Build exponential tables and use a scaled graph to read initial values and growth or decay thresholds.
lessons.before: A nonzero base raised to the zero power gives one, and a negative index gives a reciprocal.
lessons.ideas:
At \(x=0\), \(b^0=1\) and the output is \(a+c\). Negative inputs may give fractional values. Retain these until plotting.

The amount at time zero sets the first point. To model halving each hour, use a factor of \(\frac12\) per hour, or a power \(2^{-t}\).

Trace down to the time axis. Give a number with its time unit and a precision supported by the axis divisions.
lessons.method:
How do I build a shifted exponential table?

In \(y=ab^x+c\), the variable is in the exponent. Compute the power, then multiply by a and add c.

How does a repeated multiplier appear on a graph?

In a simple growth model, the amount is multiplied by the same factor greater than one each time unit. In decay the multiplier lies between zero and one.

How do I estimate when the model reaches a threshold?

Find the threshold on the vertical scale and draw the horizontal guide. The crossing identifies when the model first attains the threshold.
mistakes: A constant outside the exponent does not change the base or the exponent.
Halving subtracts different amounts from different starting values. A curve is needed to show the decay model.
The threshold itself is an amount, not a time. Its numerical value does not belong on the horizontal axis.

examples.title: Complete a shifted exponential table
examples.question:
Complete the missing entries in the table for \(y=\frac{1}{2}\times 2^{x}+2\).

\(x\)\(-2\)\(-1\)\(0\)\(1\)\(2\)
\(y\)\(\frac{17}{8}\)?\(\frac{5}{2}\)?\(4\)
examples.solution:
Evaluate the base to the given power first, multiply by the coefficient, then add the shift. A negative power gives a reciprocal.

For \(x=-1\), substitute that input into the rule. It gives \(y=\frac{9}{4}\).

For \(x=1\), substitute that input into the rule. It gives \(y=3\).

\(x\)\(-2\)\(-1\)\(0\)\(1\)\(2\)
\(y\)\(\frac{17}{8}\)\(\frac{9}{4}\)\(\frac{5}{2}\)\(3\)\(4\)

examples.title: Plot an exponential decay model
examples.question:
Complete the missing entries in the table for \(M=8\times 2^{-t}\) for the mass in grams remaining t hours after a process begins.

\(t\)\(0\)\(1\)\(2\)\(3\)
\(M\)?\(4\)?\(1\)
examples.solution:
Each whole hour halves the current mass. The curve falls as time increases.

For \(t=0\), substitute that input into the rule. It gives \(M=8\).

For \(t=2\), substitute that input into the rule. It gives \(M=2\).

\(t\)\(0\)\(1\)\(2\)\(3\)
\(M\)\(8\)\(4\)\(2\)\(1\)

examples.title: Read a threshold from a decay curve
examples.question: The graph models the mass \(M=9\times 2^{-t}\) in grams remaining after t hours. Estimate the time at which the mass falls to 3 g, to one decimal place.
examples.solution:
Move from the height \(M=3\) to the curve before reading time.

Project the intersection onto the t-axis. The reading is approximately \(1.6\) hours.

questions.title: Complete a table for an increasing straight line
questions.prompt_html:
Complete the missing entries in the table for \(y=5x+4\).

\(x\)\(-2\)\(-1\)\(0\)\(1\)\(2\)
\(y\)\(-6\)?\(4\)?\(14\)
questions.solution_html:
Multiply the x-value by the coefficient of x, then add the constant.

For \(x=-1\), substitute that input into the rule. It gives \(y=-1\).

For \(x=1\), substitute that input into the rule. It gives \(y=9\).

\(x\)\(-2\)\(-1\)\(0\)\(1\)\(2\)
\(y\)\(-6\)\(-1\)\(4\)\(9\)\(14\)
questions.hint_html: Substitute the x-value into every term of the expression. Retain the sign when using a negative input.

marking_criteria.description_html: Give the complete correct answer. At \(x=-1\), \(y=-1\), At \(x=1\), \(y=9\).

questions.title: Complete a table for an increasing straight line
questions.prompt_html:
Complete the missing entries in the table for \(y=2x+5\).

\(x\)\(-2\)\(-1\)\(0\)\(1\)\(2\)
\(y\)\(1\)?\(5\)?\(9\)
questions.solution_html:
Multiply the x-value by the coefficient of x, then add the constant.

For \(x=-1\), substitute that input into the rule. It gives \(y=3\).

For \(x=1\), substitute that input into the rule. It gives \(y=7\).

\(x\)\(-2\)\(-1\)\(0\)\(1\)\(2\)
\(y\)\(1\)\(3\)\(5\)\(7\)\(9\)
questions.hint_html: Substitute the x-value into every term of the expression. Retain the sign when using a negative input.

marking_criteria.description_html: Give the complete correct answer. At \(x=-1\), \(y=3\), At \(x=1\), \(y=7\).

questions.title: Use negative inputs for a falling line
questions.prompt_html:
Complete the missing entries in the table for \(y=-5x+5\).

\(x\)\(-2\)\(-1\)\(0\)\(1\)\(2\)
\(y\)?\(10\)\(5\)\(0\)?
questions.solution_html:
Bracket a negative input. The product of two negative numbers is positive.

For \(x=-2\), substitute that input into the rule. It gives \(y=15\).

For \(x=2\), substitute that input into the rule. It gives \(y=-5\).

\(x\)\(-2\)\(-1\)\(0\)\(1\)\(2\)
\(y\)\(15\)\(10\)\(5\)\(0\)\(-5\)
questions.hint_html: Substitute the x-value into every term of the expression. Retain the sign when using a negative input.

marking_criteria.description_html: Give the complete correct answer. At \(x=-2\), \(y=15\), At \(x=2\), \(y=-5\).

questions.title: Use negative inputs for a falling line
questions.prompt_html:
Complete the missing entries in the table for \(y=-6x+6\).

\(x\)\(-2\)\(-1\)\(0\)\(1\)\(2\)
\(y\)?\(12\)\(6\)\(0\)?
questions.solution_html:
Bracket a negative input. The product of two negative numbers is positive.

For \(x=-2\), substitute that input into the rule. It gives \(y=18\).

For \(x=2\), substitute that input into the rule. It gives \(y=-6\).

\(x\)\(-2\)\(-1\)\(0\)\(1\)\(2\)
\(y\)\(18\)\(12\)\(6\)\(0\)\(-6\)

questions.title: Read the vertical value on a straight line
questions.prompt_html: The graph shows \(y=4x-5\). Read the value of \(y\) at \(x=2\).
questions.solution_html:
Find \(x=2\) on the horizontal scale.

Move vertically to the graph and then horizontally to the vertical scale. The point is \(\left(2,3\right)\).
questions.hint_html: Start at the given input on the horizontal axis. Read the other coordinate at the graph.

questions.title: Read the vertical value on a straight line
questions.prompt_html: The graph shows \(y=x-6\). Read the value of \(y\) at \(x=1\).
questions.solution_html:
Find \(x=1\) on the horizontal scale.

Move vertically to the graph and then horizontally to the vertical scale. The point is \(\left(1,-5\right)\).
questions.hint_html: Start at the given input on the horizontal axis. Read the other coordinate at the graph.

questions.title: Read the input at a stated level
questions.prompt_html: The graph shows \(y=-2x+5\). Use the graph to find \(x\) when \(y=3\).
questions.solution_html:
Read the vertical axis at \(y=3\).

Move horizontally to the graph, then down or up to the x-axis. The reading is \(x=1\).
questions.hint_html: Start from the given height on the vertical axis.

questions.title: Read the input at a stated level
questions.prompt_html: The graph shows \(y=-3x+6\). Use the graph to find \(x\) when \(y=9\).
questions.solution_html:
Read the vertical axis at \(y=9\).

Move horizontally to the graph, then down or up to the x-axis. The reading is \(x=-1\).
questions.hint_html: Start from the given height on the vertical axis.

questions.title: Recognise the constant value shown on a grid
questions.prompt_html: Choose the equation of the plotted line.
questions.solution_html:
Every plotted input shares the height \(5\).

The equation is \(y=5\). This is a horizontal line.
questions.hint_html: Read which coordinate stays constant as you move along the line.

questions.title: Recognise the constant value shown on a grid
questions.prompt_html: Choose the equation of the plotted line.
questions.solution_html:
Every plotted input shares the height \(6\).

The equation is \(y=6\). This is a horizontal line.
questions.hint_html: Read which coordinate stays constant as you move along the line.

questions.title: Complete and plot two linear tables
questions.prompt_html:
1. Complete the missing entries in the table for \(y=5x+2\).

    \(x\)\(-2\)\(-1\)\(0\)\(1\)\(2\)
    \(y\)\(-8\)?\(2\)?\(12\)

    Then plot the graph on the grid for \(-2\leq x\leq 2\).

    [4]

  2. Complete the missing entries in the table for \(y=-5x+3\).

    \(x\)\(-2\)\(-1\)\(0\)\(1\)\(2\)
    \(y\)?\(8\)\(3\)\(-2\)?

    Then plot the graph on the grid for \(-2\leq x\leq 2\).
